newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court charges Islamic sect members.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court charges Islamic sect members.

text.p: A Turkish security court on Thursday charged 121 members of a purist Islamic sect with "terrorism" after they were detained at a rowdy religious service, Anatolian news agency said.
It said Ankara State Security Court charged the followers of the Aczimendi sect under article 7 of the anti-terror law, which forbids violent acts aimed at undermining the state.
They face between three and ten years in jail.
Most of the 121 were arrested at a service at Ankara's main Kocatepe mosque on the October 20 anniversary of the death of religious leader Said-i Nursi Bediuzzaman, who died in 1960.

Television news footage showed the Aczimendis fighting with police who tried to break up a "zikir" ceremony in which the sect members work themselves into a frenzy through communal dancing and chanting.
The Aczimendis, a small sect based in the eastern city of Elazig, dress in dark robes and turbans and carry long staffs in what they say is imitation of the Prophet Mohammed.
The vast majority of Turks wear Western-style clothing. The group shuns modern technology which it regards as unislamic.
